q: Write the general solution of \(y'' + 2y' + y = 0\).
steps: A repeated root needs the extra factor of \(x\): \(y = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{-1x}\).

traps.why: Those two terms collapse into one constant — a repeated root needs x·e^{rx} as the independent second solution.
The discriminant is zero: one root, twice. There is no second distinct root.

q: For \(y'' + 5y' + 6y = e^{2x}\), what is the correct FORM of the particular solution (undetermined coefficients)? (Note: the characteristic roots are \(-2, -3\).)
steps: Match the guess to the forcing term: exponential → \(Ae^{kx}\); polynomial → same-degree polynomial; sine/cosine → BOTH \(A\cos + B\sin\).
No resonance here: 2 is not a characteristic root \((-2, -3)\), so no extra factor of \(x\).

traps.why: The guess mirrors the forcing function’s family — exponential begets exponential, sine begets sine AND cosine.
The x-factor is only added when the forcing matches a characteristic root (resonance) — not the case here.

traps.why: ω is the SQUARE ROOT of k/m — the characteristic roots are ±√(k/m)·i.
Divide by the mass first: ω² = k/m, then take the root.
